title: Finance & Legal: End-to-End Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Policy (2026)
author: Amina Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood Inference's integrated finance-and-legal policy covering annual budgeting and quarterly forecasting, contract intake and review, procurement and purchase-order (PO) controls, and revenue recognition & billing rules. It is intended for finance (FP&A, Accounting), Legal, Procurement, People Ops (for headcount), and Engineering/Product budget owners.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference legal entities and product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Covers: annual budget cycle, rolling forecasts, contract approval matrix, procurement and PO workflow, vendor selection, revenue recognition principles, invoicing cadence, and collections/dunning.

1) Principles and Objectives:
- Accuracy: Budgets and forecasts must be supportable with assumptions and reconciled to headcount plans and capacity costs.
- Controls: Segregation of duties for approvals, PO issuance, and payments; minimum documentation standards for every contract and commitment.
- Compliance: GAAP-compliant revenue recognition and adherence to contract terms, data residency, and customer confidentiality clauses.
- Efficiency: Lean procurement processes to enable rapid product development while protecting cash flow and risk.

2) Budgeting & Forecasting Process (Owner: FP&A)
Overview:
- Annual budget prepared by FP&A in collaboration with product, engineering, SRE, go-to-market, and people-ops. Budget "lock" occurs in November for the following fiscal year.
- Rolling 4-quarter forecast updated monthly; reforecast and sensitivity runs at quarter close or material variance (>10% vs plan).
Key artifacts:
- Budget workbook (managed in Finance drive) with P&L, headcount plan, capex plan, and runway model.
- Budget assumptions memo (must include model unit economics: cost-per-1k-tokens, average model latency tier costs, reserved capacity commitments).

Timeline (annual):
1. July\u2013Aug: Strategic planning and headcount requests (people-ops + Hiring managers).
2. Sept\u2013Oct: Department budget submissions to FP&A.
3. Nov 1\u201315: Finance consolidation and executive review.
4. Nov 20: Executive approval and budget lock.
5. Dec: Budget published and operationalized into OKRs.

Forecast cadence and thresholds:
- Monthly rolling forecast maintained; any single-line-item variance >$250k or >10% requires variance memo and CFO sign-off.
- Scenario: Model cost delta >15% triggers immediate engagement with Serving Runtime and Infra for optimization/quantization analysis.

3) Contract Intake and Legal Review (Owner: Legal / Commercial Legal Ops)
Contract types:
- Standard SaaS Order Forms (hosted API subscriptions)
- Dedicated / Private deployment agreements (including SLAs and on-prem annexes)
- Professional Services statements of work (SOWs)
- Vendor master agreements (vendors, partners, resellers)
- Data processing agreements (DPAs) and security addenda

Approval matrix (effective 2026):
- Contracts <= $5,000 / one-off purchase: Manager approval (no Legal required).
- Contracts > $5,000 and <= $50,000: Department head approval + Procurement notification; Legal optional for template terms.
- Contracts > $50,000 and <= $250,000: Department head + Legal review + FP&A budget confirmation.
- Contracts > $250,000: Legal + FP&A + VP-level exec approval. All Dedicated/Private contracts (any value) require Legal review.

Required documentation (Contract Intake ticket must include):
1. Counterparty legal entity name and primary contact.
2. Contract type and proposed term (start/end dates).
3. Financial terms (MSRP, discounts, billing cadence).
4. Data residency and security requirements (if customer requests).
5. Routing for signature and post-signature owner.

Contract review SLAs:
- Standard order forms: Legal turnaround target 3 business days.
- Custom terms or DPAs: Target 7\u201310 business days; priority escalations for enterprise deals.

Templates and mandatory clauses:
- Use Finance-approved templates for Order Forms, SOWs, and Reseller agreements. Mandatory clauses include: limitation of liability (capped to fees paid in prior 12 months), IP ownership, confidentiality, data processing language per security standards, and termination for convenience notice periods.

4) Procurement & PO Workflow (Owner: Procurement / Finance Ops)
Preferred procurement tools: Coupa (or approved procurement system), integrated with Accounting (NetSuite).
Procurement steps (standard purchases):
1. Requestor creates requisition in Coupa with business justification and budget code.
2. Department approver (manager) approves requisition.
3. Procurement validates vendor (vendor due diligence for first-time vendors) and issues PO.
4. Goods/services delivered; requester confirms receipt.
5. Vendor invoice routed to AP and matched to PO for payment.

Vendor due diligence checklist (first-time vendors):
- W-9 or equivalent entity documentation.
- Sanctions screening (OFAC/SDN).
- Insurance certificates for service vendors >$50k annual spend.
- Security questionnaire if vendor will access customer data or infrastructure.

Approval thresholds and payment terms:
- < $5k: P-card or direct charge permitted.
- $5k\u2013$50k: PO required, standard 30 net payment terms unless negotiated.
- > $50k: Procurement and FP&A approval; preferred 45\u201360 day terms for capital/large purchases to preserve cash.

Procurement exceptions:
- Emergency purchases (SRE/Infra) under $25k: documented post-facto with SOC/Director approval within 3 business days.

5) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy (Owner: Accounting)
Revenue recognition principles (GAAP + ASC 606 guidance):
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue as services are provided (over time). Metered usage billed monthly in arrears. A contract exists if customer has an order form or subscription.
- Subscriptions (monthly/annual): Recognize ratably over the subscription term. For annual upfront prepayments, defer revenue and amortize monthly over the service period.
- Dedicated capacity / Reserved commitment: If customer prepays for reserved capacity, recognize ratably over the commitment period; any non-refundable setup fees are amortized over the expected benefit period (typically 12 months) unless facts indicate otherwise.
- Professional services (SOW): Recognize at completion of performance obligations. If multiple deliverables exist, allocate transaction price to performance obligations and recognize as satisfied (over time or at a point in time) per contract terms.
- Credits and refunds: Customer credits for service quality issues per SLA are recorded as contra-revenue when probable and estimable.

Billing rules and cadence:
- Standard customers: Monthly invoices generated on the 3rd business day following month-end; payment terms net 30 unless otherwise negotiated.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: Invoicing cadence per contract (monthly, quarterly, or annual). Invoices for committed usage are due per contract schedule; overages billed in arrears.
- Prepaid credits: Apply to usage first; report residual balances on balance sheet as customer deposits.

Sample revenue recognition scenarios:
- Customer A purchases $120k annual hosted plan prepaid on Jan 1: Defer $120k as unearned revenue and recognize $10k/month Jan\u2013Dec.
- Customer B uses metered API and consumes $4,500 in January: Recognize $4,500 revenue for January and invoice in February.

Collections and dunning:
- Day 0: Invoice issued.
- Day 8: Reminder email.
- Day 30: Past due notice; account flagged for sales/CS outreach.
- Day 45: Second notice; finance places payment hold and initiates phone collections.
- Day 60: Escalation to Legal for contract enforcement and collections; potential suspension of service per contract terms.
- Late fee policy: 1.5% monthly on past-due balances after 30 days unless prohibited by contract or law.

6) Accounting Close & Reporting Controls (Owner: Accounting)
- Monthly close checklist with reconciliations for deferred revenue, AR aging, vendor accruals, and capital expenditures.
- Key controls: 2-person approval for journal entries > $50k; monthly reconciliation sign-off by Accounting Manager; quarterly review of revenue recognition estimates by Controller.
- Audit readiness: Maintain contract repository with scanned signed contracts and order forms; link contracts to revenue schedules in the accounting system.

7) Ownership, Escalation, and Exceptions
- Owners:
  - FP&A: Budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis.
  - Accounting: Revenue recognition rules, billing cadence, month-end close.
  - Legal: Contract templates, NDAs, DPAs, and review SLAs.
  - Procurement: Vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and vendor performance management.

- Escalation paths:
  - Budget variances > $250k: FP&A -> CFO.
  - Contractual/legal risk (data residency / indemnity): Legal -> GC.
  - Procurement disputes > $50k: Procurement -> VP Finance.

- Exceptions: All exceptions must be recorded in the finance exception log and require written approval from FP&A and Legal (if contract-related).

8) Examples & Templates (Appendix)
- Template locations: Finance drive / Contracts drive (links maintained in the contract intake tool).
- Example JEs: "Debit AR, Credit Revenue" for billed usage; "Debit Cash, Credit Deferred Revenue" for prepayments.
- Sample SLA credit calculation table: 99.9% uptime = 0% credit; 99.0\u201399.9% = 5% credit; <99.0% = 10% credit (see SLA appendix for full policy).
